subject: Numerical integration with model parameters as input

messages.author: 88e347d23ce0b341
messages.subject: Numerical integration with model parameters as input
parts:
Hi,

I have a complex likelihood where the form of the mean includes an integral of some function f(x,a,b) over values of x which come from the input data where a and b are fixed and are model parameters.

I've found this documentation on numerical integration: https://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/namespacegauss__kronrod.html#ad2a3bebe64e675f09612aa6211ef1998.

But I can't figure out how to correctly define the integrand here. One thought I had is to define a univariate function of x inside the function where a and b are defined, but C++ doesn't appear to like nested functions.

Here's a toy example for this helper function which does not compile:
template<class Type>
Type mu(Type x, Type a, Type b) {
  using gauss_kronrod::integrate;
  Type f(Type xnew){
    return a+b*xnew;
  }
  Type result = integrate(f, x, x+1);
  return result;
}

Thank you in advance for the help and advice!
Katie

messages.subject: Re: Numerical integration with model parameters as input
parts:
Copying the example from https://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/namespaceromberg.html with the romberg method:

#include <TMB.hpp>

template<class Type>
struct univariate {
  Type a, b;               // Parameter in integrand
  univariate(Type a_, Type b_)    // Constructor of integrand
  : a (a_), b (b_) {}       // Initializer list
  Type operator()(Type x){   // Evaluate integrand
    return a + b*x;
  }
};

template<class Type>
Type objective_function<Type>::operator() ()
{
PARAMETER(a);
PARAMETER(b);
PARAMETER(t);
univariate<Type> f(a, b);
Type res = romberg::integrate(f, t, t+1);
return(res);

}
